title: 1974: arriving in Los Angeles and dropping instruments in Chicago
summary: Howard recalls his arrival on the Santa Fe, with cornet, alto saxophone and trumpet, which fell from the wagon in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: I arrived in Los Angeles in the afternoon about 2:00 o'clock, on the Santa Fe Limited. I don't know whether they called it a limited at that time or not. It was a slow train coming through Chicago and where I had an accident riding one of those big buses. A big bus -- I took my -- I dropped my instruments. I had a cornet, alto saxophone, and a trumpet. Didn't call it a trumpet in those days. It was a cornet. And I was riding one of those big buses down -- I can't think of the name of the street. Let me do it like this. Can I do it like that? I can't think of the name of the street it

was coming down, but it was the main -- the main avenue that you come down in Chicago to get to the Santa Fe Station, and that's where I had to go to. And everything fell out of my lap and fell on the ground. It was quite a scramble with the man who was driving this bus. It wasn't a bus either, it was a four-Talley horse pulling a wagon. And that's where I was riding, up on top, with him. And it was quite a deal. Well, everybody give me a big laugh, but it wasn't funny to me because I had to scramble down to the ground and get my things up and pick them up and he was yelling at me to hurry up, come on, we were going to miss the train, and et cetera, et cetera, et cetera. And those kind of things hurt you, but it didn't bother me because I was a youngster full of adventure and I wanted to get to California to where my people were.
My uncle was here, my auntie and their family. Now, just a minute. Can you hold it?
